dedupe_keys.name: rapid collaborative research investigation of reinforced concrete buildings damaged in the magnitude 6 4 southern taiwan earthquake of february 2016

description: RAPID/Collaborative Research: Investigation of Reinforced Concrete Buildings Damaged in the Magnitude 6.4 Southern Taiwan Earthquake of February 2016 is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "field reconnaissance", published or maintained by Dawn Lehman, University of Washington (washington.edu). The Magnitude- 6.4 Meinong Earthquake struck the Southern region of Taiwan in February 2016. The earthquake primarily resulted in building damage. The majority of these buildings had reinforced concrete frames as the primary lateral-load resisting system. The most common damage mechanism was a soft story resulting from shear and/or flexural-shear damage to the first-story columns. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "field reconnaissance" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/DS2CP4W. Keywords: Meinong Earthquake, Building, Nonductile Concrete, Earthquake Damage, ASCE 41, Tier 1. Published 2017-01-26. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated in the DesignSafe listing (publication licences offered are CC BY 4.0, ODC-By, CC0 and GPL; project page not read). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
